econ_release_lag.title: Scheduled economic releases: how fast do Polymarket prices absorb a number that is published at a known second, and what was left for someone acting seconds or minutes later?

study.headline: Polymarket absorbs scheduled economic numbers in about 5 seconds (98% of the stale-price money is taken within 30 s, mostly by three wallets), so a taker arriving at +30 s finds at most about $7-13 a day at $500 per market, with t = 1.84 in the reporting part.
study.key_numbers:
Sample: 51 release seconds (53 release ids), 75 Polymarket events, 268 markets, 2026-09-01..11-26; reporting part from 2026-10-15 = 30 releases / 140 markets.
E1: winner's last pre-release price median 0.888; 140 of 268 markets still uncertain (<0.90).
E2 (uncertain markets): median 5 s to first print >=0.95; 76/120/128 of 140 within 5 s/30 s/2 min; per release median 4 s. By type: ISM 0 s, Michigan 1, JOLTS 2, non-US GDP 1, central banks 4, US GDP 4, CPI 6, PCE 6, PPI 7, Employment 11, FOMC 15, non-US inflation 21.
E3 (stale trades after release, all takers): $107,046 changed hands, $30,347 gap (~$350/day). Gap by time: 0-5 s $12,768; 5-30 s $16,964; 30 s-2 min $462; 2-10 min $113; later $40. 110 taker wallets, top three 46.7%, top ten 76.7%; per release median 4 wallets, top three take 100%.
E4 (winner at <=0.97, $500/market, fee 0.01, outcome known) | whole period | reporting part | t by release (reporting):
+5 s: $6,147 on $22,913 cost ($70.65/day) | $2,038 on $9,049 ($47.40/day) | 2.56 (54% of it in fills stamped +5/+6 s)
+30 s (primary): $640 on $3,692 ($7.36/day) | $570 on $3,327 ($13.25/day), fills in 11 markets / 5 releases | 1.84
+2 min: $183 ($2.11/day) | $121 ($2.81/day) | 1.40
+10 min: $76 ($0.88/day) | $74 ($1.72/day) | 1.00
At +30 s: zero fills in Employment, PPI, US GDP, FOMC, JOLTS, ISM, Michigan; $485 of the $640 comes from Germany GDP, Argentina CPI and Korea GDP; $134 from flagged markets (eggs, delayed October CPI resolution). Nothing left after 5 s in markets above $100K volume.
study.caveats:
- E4 is an upper bound, not a backtest of achievable profit: it uses the resolved outcome, so every fill is profitable by construction, and it assumes we take every print away from the taker who really got it. The t-statistics measure how regularly stale offers exist, not whether we would win them.
- The +5 s variant does clear t > 2 in the reporting part (2.56, 140 markets), but it was not the declared primary and 54% of its profit sits in fills stamped +5/+6 s, inside the 1-2 s block-time jitter. I did not call it an opportunity for that reason.
- Only prints are visible. Untaken offers and book depth are unknown, and maker behaviour (how fast quotes are pulled) cannot be seen.
- T is the scheduled second, never re-timed. For tier B publishers the clock time came from my own knowledge of their standing publication times, not from pages fetched today; the tape gate confirmed 36 of them and dropped 7 (RBNZ-sep, BOC-sep, ECB-sep, BOE-sep, SNB-sep, BOI-oct, ECB-oct; 27 markets, all fully priced, largest pre-release gap 0.09). Argentina's first reaction comes at +15 to +39 s, probably the publisher's own delay.
- bls.gov blocks direct requests (403); the BLS 2026 schedule was read through WebFetch, whose summary I could not check against the raw page. BEA and Fed calendars were fetched directly.
- Retail sales and weekly jobless claims have no Polymarket markets. China GDP was lost because the rules gave the wrong date (5 markets closed before the scheduled time). BoJ, Copom, Colombia, SARB, RBI, Bank of Korea and China CPI were excluded in advance for lack of a scheduled second.
- 39 markets were flagged in advance as needing judgement or resolving late. The October CPI annual and core y/y events stayed open ten days with the winner at about 0.95; fills there are resolution-risk carry, not a time gap.
- Fee of 0.01 was applied everywhere, including the US GDP event whose gamma field says 0; the fee history before 2026-11-20 is unverified.
- Small sample: 87 days, two FOMC meetings, three prints of each monthly US release; 52% of the +5 s profit comes from three releases and 80% of the +30 s profit from three.
- Process: the first discovery run included the `finance` tag and pulled 10,000 irrelevant events before I discarded them (heavier on the API than intended). I saw the tape of one release (September CPI) as the sanity slice before running the rest, after the protocol was fixed.
- Toolkit: `stats.ratio_cluster` gives meaningless t-values (26, 122) when only one or two clusters have non-zero cost, so the mean-per-release t is the one reported; `updown.buyable` assumes Up/Down names, so Yes/No conversion is in the study's own `lib.py`; `gamma.iter_events` needs `limit=50`. Nothing under pmlab/ was edited and NOTES.md was not touched.
ideas: Record the economy books by 1-second REST polling from T-60 s to T+120 s at the next releases (Employment 2026-12-04, FOMC 2026-12-09, CPI 2026-12-10) to see resting stale offers and how fast makers pull them.

Measure our own latency: seconds from the scheduled time until the number is readable on bls.gov, bea.gov and federalreserve.gov from a VPS, against the +3 to +6 s at which incumbents' fills are stamped.
Take the incumbent wallets apart with pmlab.wallet (0x8cb3ed, 0x059468, 0x2f633e, 0x67babd): are they profitable after wrong-bucket losses, do they quote before the release, what else do they snipe.
Maker side of the same event: resting bids on the outcome-consistent side in thin non-US markets (Germany GDP, Korea GDP, Argentina CPI), where absorption took 1-6 minutes.
Separate study of thin non-US releases at off-hours with an independently fetched calendar (Eurostat, Destatis, INDEC, Bank of Korea, NBS, BoJ), the only place anything survived 30 seconds.
Delayed-resolution carry: the October CPI events traded near 0.95 for ten days after the number; find out what the dispute was and whether such cases are systematically safe.
Pre-release side: takers at 0.40-0.60 won 49.1%, so no edge before the number; test whether nowcasts (Cleveland Fed, GDPNow) beat bucket prices in the last day.
Use the public L2 archive (chitoyuuri/polymarket-l2-v3-1-archive, category economy) to replace print-based E4 with true book depth at T+d.

problems.effect: $74 of the $570 for $1,632 held ten days under dispute risk. Fills within 2 h of T only: $540 reporting.

problems.effect: Only visible wrong-side evidence: takers who went long the eventual loser at 0.50 or more within 10 minutes lost $329 over 7 releases. E4 stays an upper bound.

crypto_levels_vs_options.title: Crypto price-level markets versus option-implied probabilities: are the gaps large and slow enough to trade with a 0.01 fee?

study.headline: The gap between Polymarket BTC/ETH threshold prices and a DVOL lognormal model is small (2-3 points, not 5-6) and mostly model error or untradable empty-book mids; after the tape check the best variant is +$694 on 43 entries (t=2.08) across only 34 markets, all from the NO side in a month when BTC fell 27%, so no tradable edge is shown.
study.key_numbers:
Universe: 560 "above at noon ET" markets (BTC 323, ETH 237; 62 asset-date clusters; tune 359 / report 201) and 825 one-touch markets, resolving 27 Oct-26 Nov, volume >= $5K.

L1 gap (market minus DVOL model, strikes with model prob 0.05-0.95, 40,866 market-hours): mean +0.005, sd 0.039, mean abs 0.024, 8.6% of hours at >= 0.05. Mean abs by horizon: 2-12h 0.041, 12-48h 0.030, >=48h 0.023. With realised 24h vol: mean abs 0.046.
L2: autocorrelation 0.65 / 0.58 / 0.47 at 1 / 4 / 12 h. Gaps >= 0.05 lose 59% in 1 h (half-life 0.8 h), then a slow tail (0.32 left at 4 h, 0.24 at 12 h). The market moves (-0.68 x gap in 4 h), the model does not.
Deribit check (BTC, 10 daily expiries): one-day ATM IV / DVOL median 1.10 (quartiles 0.96-1.27); option digitals deviate from the model with the same sign as Polymarket.
Outcome reproduction from Binance: 550/550 daily ladders, 825/825 one-touch.

L3 primary, tuned variant g=0.05, 48h-7d (period | entries | markets | clusters | PnL | return | t | $/day):
paper tune | 729 | 313 | 40 | +$4,654 | +31.9% | 2.51 | +233
paper report | 507 | 194 | 22 | +$2,664 | +26.3% | 3.96 | +242
confirmed tune | 32 | 27 | 16 | +$472 | +73.7% | 1.49 | +24
confirmed report | 43 | 34 | 15 | +$695 | +80.8% | 2.08 | +63
confirmed report, full $20 size on tape | 13 | - | - | +$47 | - | - | +4
Confirmed report by side: NO 31 entries +$704, YES 12 entries -$10; two clusters (BTC 16-17 Nov) = $497.
Other confirmed report variants (g, band: entries, PnL, t): 0.05 2-12h: 40, +$140, 0.86; 0.05 12-48h: 63, +$151, 1.38; 0.08 2-12h: 30, -$81, -1.58; 0.08 12-48h: 12, +$7, 0.20; 0.08 48h-7d: 16, +$102, 2.59; 0.12 2-12h: 16, -$19, -0.45; 0.12 12-48h: 3, -$35, -2.13; 0.12 48h-7d: 7, +$31, 0.91.

L4: 150-entry random sample 46 confirmed = 30.7% (Wilson 23.8-38.5%), 20% with full size; all 2,078 entries 22.8% confirmed (2-12h 79%, 12-48h 54%, 48h-7d 7%).
Secondary realised-vol model: confirmed tuned report 70 entries / 55 markets, +$877, t=1.78.
One-touch: mean gap -0.027, half-life 2.4-6.7 h; 36.7% of entries confirmed; confirmed report variants -17% to +2% of stake, none with abs t above 1.4.
study.caveats:
- The paper result passes the bar (report t=3.96, 194 markets) but is not real: 91.5% of those entries had no print at or below the assumed price within 10 minutes. Signals in the 48h-7d band are mostly mids of empty or wide books.
- The confirmed result is directional. All of it is NO-side exposure while BTC fell 27% and ETH 31%; the YES side lost in the tune period (1 win in 12).
- t-values at horizons above 24 h are overstated: 7-day ladders of consecutive dates overlap, so the 15-22 reporting clusters are far fewer independent bets. One month, one trend.
- A print within 10 minutes shows the price existed at some moment, not at entry and not with depth; only 13 of the 43 confirmed entries had the full $20 on the tape. No book data was used.
- The systematic gap of 0.5-1.7 points is model error (flat 30-day DVOL, no skew, about 10% too low for one-day horizons), not market error. Price source and resolution minute are correct.
- The Deribit comparison uses trade candles only (noisy, mean abs 7.7 points per spread), BTC only, at the 08:00 UTC expiry, not interpolated to noon ET.
- The 0.01 fee is assumed for the whole window; the rate before 2026-11-20 is unverified. Fees are 0.4% of stake, so the sign would not change.
- 27 variants were run, not 9: 9 primary, plus 9 with realised vol and 9 on one-touch, both declared in protocol.md before any result. The verdict uses the primary 9 only.
- The L4 check was run on the 150-entry sample as specified and also on all entries; the confirmed tables use the full check.
- While reading metadata, the resolved outcomes of one hit-price event were printed before the protocol was written; no model value or rule was involved.
- Toolkit problems, worked around in study code: gamma.iter_events default limit=100 returns HTTP 406 (use limit=50); dataapi.prices_history fails for spans above 15 days (chunked); updown.buyable/sellable assume Up/Down outcome names.
- I appended a short verified-facts section to /home/user/polymarket-lab/NOTES.md, as its own rules ask.
ideas: Maker instead of taker in the 48h-7d ladders: the gap there is an empty or wide book, so quote both sides around a smile-aware fair value and collect spread plus liquidity rewards (rewardsMinSize 50, rewardsMaxSpread 4.5). Measure spreads, fill rates and adverse selection on the HF L2 archive first.

Replace flat DVOL with Deribit's short-dated smile: poll book summaries live and interpolate total variance between the 08:00 UTC expiries around noon ET. This removes the 1-2 point skew error and the 10% vol-level error before any signal is counted.

Re-measure entry prices from recorded books (ask and depth) for the 2-48h bands, where 54-79% of signals did have prints, and test whether the tune-period loss at 2-12h means the book is ahead of the model near expiry.

Model-free consistency checks on the same ladders: monotonicity across strikes, the above ladder against the neg-risk range buckets of the same date, and bounds between 'reach K today' and 'above K at noon'.
Take the direction out: hedge with a perp sized by model delta, or re-run on a flat month, to see whether anything remains of the NO-side result.
Extend the fill check to 30-60 minutes to learn how long a displayed gap waits for a trade; if it is hours, a resting bid at the model price is the natural test.

One-touch markets trade persistently about 3 points below a continuous-barrier lognormal model, and outcomes sat between the two. A barrier model with discrete monitoring and the short-dated smile would show whether any of that is market error.

problems.issue: Size is not capped at what the tape shows. The simulation books the full $20 at the entry price whenever any print at that price exists. Median tape size at or below the entry price is 16 shares against 26.8 assumed; 16 of the 43 entries had under a quarter of the size and 9 had exactly the 5-share minimum. The three largest wins buy 160-178 NO shares at 11-12 cents where the tape shows 10, 18 and 31 shares.
problems.effect: Tuned variant, confirmed, report: +$694.5 becomes +$164.4 on $480 of stake actually on the tape (t 1.88, about +$15 a day). The top three entries go from $453.5 to $52.3. Tune period: +$471.9 becomes +$48.9 (t 0.43).

problems.issue: Fill evidence predates the entry price. The entry price is the mid of bucket t+300 plus 1 cent, but a print anywhere in (t, t+600] counts as confirmation. In 30 of the 43 entries the only qualifying print came before t+300, before the price the order is supposed to pay was observable. The window is the lab lead's wording, so the defect is inherited from the protocol.
problems.effect: Those 30 entries carry $651 of the $694.5. Prints in (t+300, t+600] only: 13 entries, +$43.9 (t 0.41), size-capped -$21.5. Prints in (t+300, t+900]: 28 entries, +$153.4 (t 1.08), size-capped +$4.9. Tune period under the same windows: -$57 and -$55. Confirmed share in the 48h-7d band falls from 7.0% to 2.8-4.5%.

problems.issue: The tune/report split leaks. Markets are assigned by resolution date, but a ladder trades for 7 days before resolving, so report entries start on 9 Nov while tune outcomes run to 15 Nov. 18 of the 43 report entries were signalled before the last tune market resolved; the variant was chosen on outcomes produced by the same BTC path (75.1K on 9 Nov to 64.7K on 15 Nov) and not yet known at those entries.
problems.effect: Those 18 entries make +$647.4. The 25 entries made after the tune period ended make +$47.2 (t 0.43); size-capped -$19.5.

problems.issue: The t-value is measured against zero, the wrong benchmark in a month with BTC down 27%. A placebo with the same band, entry price and tape rule but no gap condition: blind NO earned +94% on stake in the report period (980 entries, 185 markets) and +102% in the tune period; blind YES lost 59% and 50%. The signal earned +81% overall and +114% on its NO side, with 72% of entries on NO.
problems.effect: Excess of the 43 entries over blind buying of the same side: -$322 against the same resolution ladder (t -1.06), -$1,470 against the same market at a random confirmable time (t -1.69), +$250 against the same period (t 0.75). Tune: +$85 to +$183, t 0.4-0.6. If the model were exactly right the 43 entries would be worth +$40; they made +$694, so at least nine tenths is the price path.

problems.issue: Concentration: ten markets make $737 of the $694.5 and three entries make $453.5.
problems.effect: Without the best ten markets: 29 entries, -$42.1 (t -0.52). Without the best resolution date: +$379.5 (t 1.81). Clustered by resolution date with BTC and ETH together t is 1.90; by entry day 1.76.

problems.issue: The rule does not check that the gap still exists at the entry bucket. Only 14 of the 43 report entries still had a 0.05 gap at t+300. One entry buys YES at 0.774 with the model at 0.571. Mean model edge at the entry price is 2.3 cents a share.
problems.effect: The 29 entries whose gap was already gone carry $416. Most confirmed entries are not trades on a 5-point gap; among paper entries 44-48% of gaps are gone one bucket later.

problems.issue: The Deribit check (c) does not support the weight put on it. The model uses Binance BTCUSDT as the forward for options settled on the USD index, a basis NOTES.md warns about (Binance was $51 above the Deribit index when I checked). The signature is in the analyst's own data: near-the-money implied vol over DVOL is 1.00 from calls and 1.20 from puts. Agreement in the outer buckets is what clipping a noisy spread estimate to [0,1] produces.
problems.effect: With the forward lowered by $51-73 the option digital sits 4.2-5.0 points above the lognormal model in the 0.3-0.7 bucket (analyst: 2.6), while Polymarket is 1.4 above it. So 'the systematic gap is model error' is not established, and '2-3 points, not 5-6' is a distance to a flat-vol model, not to option prices. The pooled vol ratio of 1.10 survives. No effect on any PnL figure.

problems.issue: gamma volumeNum is shares, not dollars (tape shares equal it in 532 of 532 markets). The 'volume >= $5K' universe includes 104 of 532 taped markets with under $5,000 of turnover, 50 under $2,000. The filter also uses final volume, which is unknown at entry time; it dropped 132 of 682 daily markets, 105 of them ETH.
problems.effect: On the headline: 1 of the 34 confirmed markets is under $5,000; without it 42 entries, +$675.8. The universe description in results.md overstates dollar volume by a factor of about 2.4.

problems.issue: The fee rate before 20 Nov is assumed to be 0.01; the tape has no fee field and I did not measure it from a wallet.
problems.effect: At 0.07 the report figure would be +$676.6 instead of +$694.5. The sign does not change.

problems.issue: One-touch group: 5 signals are dropped because the entry bucket fell after the barrier was hit.
problems.effect: -$58 on the tune period had they been entered. The one-touch conclusion (no edge) is unchanged.

problems.issue: The pooled 'all distinct confirmed' figures (+$1,249 tune, +$967 report) reuse liquidity: 9 entries share their 10-minute window with another entry of the same market and side, and 145 sit within 12 h of one.
problems.effect: Those pooled figures are descriptive only, as the analyst says; the tuned variant itself uses no print twice.

- Rule: 3,352 entries (2,078 distinct) matched one to one, PnL identical to 1e-14; 473 confirmed, same entries; all 18 confirmed cells identical.
- Protocol sample: 46 of 150 confirmed, 30 with full size.
